## Blocks

| `error.try` (statement) | `try %TRY catch %ERROR as %NAME %CATCH catch …` | `try { %TRY } catch (const %ERROR& %NAME) { %CATCH } …` | Runs the blocks after try. If one of them throws an error, the first catch part for that kind of error runs, with the error in its variable; the parts are tried in order, and std::exception catches every kind. Add catch parts with ⊕ and remove them with ⊖. | `ERROR0`, `ERROR1`, …: a type, `std::exception`, `std::invalid_argument`, `std::out_of_range` or `std::runtime_error`, default `std::exception`, one for each of `catchCount`. `NAME0`, `NAME1`, …: the name of the new variable, one for each of `catchCount`. | `TRY`: blocks. `CATCH0`, `CATCH1`, …: blocks, one for each of `catchCount`. Setting `catchCount`: 1 to 8, default 1. |
| `error.throw` (statement) | `throw %ERROR with message %MESSAGE` | `throw %ERROR(%MESSAGE);` | Stops the blocks here with an error of this kind and this message. The nearest try block around it that catches the kind runs its catch part next; with none, the program stops. | `ERROR`: a type, `std::runtime_error`, `std::invalid_argument` or `std::out_of_range`, default `std::runtime_error`. | `MESSAGE`: text; default `"Something went wrong."`. |
| `error.message` (reporter, gives `std::string`) | `message of %ERROR` | `%ERROR.what()` | The message of an error that a catch part caught. | `ERROR`: the variable it uses. | — |
| `error.rethrow` (statement) | `throw the error again` | `throw;` | Throws the error this catch part caught again, for a try block further out to catch. It can only be used inside a catch part. | — | — |
